sections.title: How to Convert Drum MIDI Between Engines | Drumverter
sections.description: Convert drum MIDI between GetGood Drums, EZdrummer, Superior Drummer, Addictive Drums and 80+ engines in four steps, free and in your browser.

p: Drumverter is a free drum MIDI remapper for every sample engine. It converts a drum MIDI groove written for one sample engine's note layout into another's — entirely in your browser. Drop in a .mid from GetGood Drums, remap it to EZdrummer, Superior Drummer 3, Addictive Drums 2, General MIDI, or Guitar Pro, and download a ready-to-use file. No upload, no signup, no cost — your files never leave your machine.

steps.title: Add your files.
steps.body: Drop one or more .mid files anywhere on the page, or click to choose.

steps.title: Pick source and target.
steps.body: Choose the engine your MIDI was written for and the engine you want it mapped to.

steps.title: Fine-tune (optional).
steps.body: Open the note editor to change which note each drum plays, or which drum a note in your file triggers.

steps.title: Download.
steps.body: Get a single .mid, or a .zip when you convert several at once.

note.title: Save a preset (optional).
note.body: Use Save as preset in the editor to keep a source→target pair, with any note changes you made. It appears under the engine lists as a chip — one click reloads it, ✎ reopens it in the editor, and the ⋯ menu renames, duplicates, or deletes it. Presets stay in this browser.

p: Drumverter maps between dozens of drum-engine note layouts, in any direction — including:

list: GetGood Drums (Invasion, Modern & Massive, and more)
Native Instruments Studio Drummer & Abbey Road

p: Every mapping goes through a canonical drum vocabulary with per-slot fallbacks, so a note with no exact match falls back to the closest available voice instead of being dropped.

sections.heading: Frequently asked questions
sections.title: Drum MIDI Converter FAQ | Drumverter
sections.description: Answers about Drumverter: cost, privacy, octave conventions (C-1 vs C-2), batch conversion and what happens to drums with no equivalent.

faq.a: Yes. It runs entirely in your browser, with no account and no cost.

faq.q: Do my MIDI files get uploaded?
faq.a: No. Conversion happens locally in your browser; files never leave your device.

faq.q: How do I convert GetGood Drums MIDI to EZdrummer?
faq.a: Add the .mid, set the source to GetGood Drums and the target to EZdrummer, then download the remapped file.

faq.q: Which DAWs and octave conventions are supported?
faq.a: Both common note-octave conventions are covered — toggle between C-1 (Reaper, Logic, Ableton, Guitar Pro) and C-2 (Studio One, Cubase, FL Studio) so note names match your DAW.

faq.q: Can I convert multiple files at once?
faq.a: Yes. Queue several .mid files and download them all as a single .zip.

faq.q: What if a drum has no equivalent in the target engine?
faq.a: Drumverter uses per-slot fallback chains to pick the closest available voice, and reports anything it couldn't map.
